title: Machine computing canonical serialization
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet and a function $T\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that, on every Boolean input string $x$, the machine halts after exactly $T(|x|)$ steps and outputs the serialization of the machine decoded from $x$.
hypotheses_covered: existence of a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
existence of a time-bound function $T\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$
computation on every Boolean input string $x$
output is the serialization of the decoded machine
replaced:
There exist a finite Turing machine over the two-letter Boolean alphabet and a time
bound $T \colon \bbn \to \bbn$ such that on every Boolean string the machine halts
within $T$ of the input's length, outputting the fixed serialization of the
one-work-tape binary machine that the string decodes to (malformed strings decoding
to the trivial one-state halting machine).
